title: Reload+Reload: Exploiting Cache and Memory Contention Side Channel on AMD SEV
problem: AMD Secure Encrypted Virtualization (SEV) is designed to protect guest VMs in multi-tenant clouds via memory encryption, but two previously unknown side channels—cache flush timing and memory contention—expose information even through the SEV-SNP isolation boundary.
motivation: Cloud TEE (Trusted Execution Environment) solutions like AMD SEV are deployed in production to guard sensitive workloads, making any new cross-VM side channel a critical security threat that undermines encrypted VM isolation.
method: The authors identify two new timing-based information leaks in AMD systems: cache flush timing (how fast the CPU cache clears) and memory block contention (delays when VMs compete for memory). They develop Reload+Reload attacks—methods that repeatedly load data and measure response times—to expose memory access patterns from other VMs, replacing the disabled Flush+Reload technique. The cache-timing variant creates a covert channel (hidden communication path) for Spectre attacks (a CPU exploit that reads secrets), while the memory-contention variant extracts AES-128 encryption keys by measuring memory response delays even though the VMs are isolated by SEV-SNP.
key_novelty: Two new timing-based side channels in AMD systems—cache flush timing (measuring how long the CPU cache takes to clear) and memory block contention (timing when VMs compete for memory access)—enable Reload+Reload attacks that break through SEV-SNP isolation and outperform Prime+Probe by being more reliable under system noise and leaking information faster.
contributions: Identification of two previously unknown side channels in AMD processors with SEV/SEV-SNP support.
Construction of two Reload+Reload attack variants (RRFS, RRMB) exploiting these channels against SEV-SNP VMs.
Demonstration of a Spectre covert channel with superior noise resistance over Prime+Probe using RRFS.
Successful AES-128 secret key extraction from SEV-SNP protected VMs using RRMB.

metrics.other: RRFS covert channel demonstrates superior noise resistance and higher capacity than Prime+Probe; AES-128 key fully extracted

limitations: Not discussed; applicability to non-AMD platforms or future hardware mitigations is not addressed.
primary_theme: Cache and memory contention side-channel attacks on AMD SEV-SNP
